Definition: from the perfect tense of G2476; to be stationary, i.e. (figuratively) to persevere:--stand (fast).
BiblicalUsage: Stand fast is the apostle's order, and it comes in three forms: watch ye, stand fast in the faith, quit you like men, be strong; stand fast therefore in the liberty wherewith Christ hath made us free; and so stand fast in the Lord, my dearly beloved.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe standing fast is the whole of the Christian's posture: watch, hold the liberty, and stand in the Lord.
